brief.answer: Whether to swap 4 USDC to EURC depends on your currency needs, not on a yield or price opportunity. EURC tracks the euro 1:1 and USDC tracks the US dollar 1:1 — both issued by Circle with identical reserve structures [3][4]. At today's rate, 4 USDC would convert to roughly 3.50 EURC (based on the ~0.874 EURC per USDC rate shown by SimpleSwap [1]), reflecting the current EUR/USD exchange rate. The swap makes sense only if you want euro-denominated exposure — for example, if you earn, spend, or report in euros and want to eliminate USD/EUR forex risk [2][5]. If your obligations are in dollars, staying in USDC is correct. Note: the swap fee on Arc is priced separately and is not stated in the available sources — do not factor an estimated fee into this decision.
brief.reasoning: The decision is purely a currency-exposure question, not a return-seeking one [2][3]. EURC and USDC are functionally identical except for their peg currency [4]. The current rate of ~0.874 EURC per USDC [1] simply reflects the live EUR/USD rate; swapping gains you euro denomination and removes dollar risk if your liabilities are in euros [5][6]. For a 4 USDC position the FX exposure is small in absolute terms, but the principle is the same: swap only if your spending or reporting currency is euros. Arc's swap fee is not quoted in any of the supplied sources, so no cost-benefit estimate can be made on that dimension.
